A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Dysca and retain its central benchmark framework. The main texts, tables, figures, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 10 LVLM checkpoints, including perceptual-task scores, attack robustness, benchmark correlations, and evaluation-size stability experiments.

after.justification: v3 reports an expanded 26-model main comparison and original blind evaluations, clustering analyses, distribution comparisons, and dataset correctness and safety audits.

M1.justification: v3 Section 3.3 extends the stated construction procedure with rejection using the top six LVLMs and subsequent removal of problematic metadata vocabulary and associated samples. v1 already included manual metadata screening and CLIP/OCR filtering, but not these additional components. The reported filtering rate changes from approximately 15% to 40%, while the underlying image and rule-based question generation remains.

E1.justification: The 20 Dysca subtasks, 51 styles, and four image scenarios remain. v3 adds a text-only test scenario, including LLaVA comparisons on MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, and MathVista in Appendix D. Its new distribution analysis also uses additional image collections, including CCBench, COCO-Val, MMVet, MME, and MMStar.

E2.justification: The main comparison expands from 10 checkpoints to 26 entries, adding methods including XComposer2-VL, GLM-4V, MiniCPM-V2.5, Yi-VL, mPLUG-Owl-2, Phi-3-Vision, GPT-4o, and Gemini-1.5-Pro. Additional BLIP2, InstructBLIP, and MiniGPT configurations are evaluated. v1's separate Shikra-VQA entry is absent from the corresponding principal comparison, although it remains in the retained stability plot.

E3.justification: v3 introduces SQ/SC evaluation metrics and image-withholding controls. New protocols include CLIP-feature KMMD comparisons using an RBF kernel and up to 3,000 images per benchmark, plus a 7.7K-image manual audit. Tables also revise Shikra's stated language backbone from Vicuna-7B to LLaMA-7B. Averaging the three question-type scores already appeared in v1 Appendix A and is not a new protocol.

E4.justification: v3 adds hierarchical inter-task and animal-category analyses, blind controls, distribution comparisons, and new failure cases. Appendix C audits 7.7K images, identifies 167 problematic images, and measures the effect of excluding them; Appendix B adds a NudeNet safety audit. These substantially extend validation beyond v1's correlations and size-stability analysis. The original stability analysis remains, while the detailed 51-style heatmap analysis is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The new SQ/SC variances measure performance variation across question types and styles, rather than uncertainty in estimated performance. The retained stability plot also provides no uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Many retained-model values change: BLIP2/Flan-T5-XL's clean style TF accuracy is 88.62 in v1 Table 3 and 35.45 in v3 Table 8. v3 adds expanded rankings and blind, sensitivity, KMMD, and audit results, while omitting some question-format and noisy-subtask breakdowns. The correlation coefficients in v1 Table 5 and v3 Table 4 are identical. Revised cleaning prevents treating updated scores as established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: v3 Section 3.4 adds mathematical definitions of chance-normalized question-type sensitivity SQ and across-style sensitivity SC in Equations 1–2. These are new metric definitions, absent from v1, but constitute a limited mathematical extension without accompanying theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion broaden the reported empirical contribution from eight open-source model families with 10 checkpoints to 24 open-source entries and two closed-source models. The central claims about dynamic, scalable synthetic generation, perceptual coverage, and the validity of synthetic evaluation remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations linking performance to language-model capacity, question-type sensitivity to language-model biases, commercial-model responses to safety training, and marine-animal weaknesses to training-data scarcity. It also interprets blind, KMMD, and audit findings as evidence of fairness and reliability. v1's detailed common-versus-uncommon-style interpretation disappears. The existing limitation concerning rule-based generation of cognition questions remains.

D1.justification: v3 discloses the CLIP filtering threshold of 0.75, adds visual-encoder identifiers and evaluation JSON examples in Appendix I, and specifies details of the new audits. The repository address changes from Benchmark-Dysca/Dysca to Robin-WZQ/Dysca, and the datasheet supplies creator and maintainer/contact information. Hardware and licensing disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting newer models, statistical tools, label-error comparisons, and safety auditing, and briefly discusses commercial LVLM APIs. The principal benchmark taxonomy and positioning of Dysca against existing-image benchmarks and JourneyDB remain. The introduction more explicitly presents the annotation-cost comparison with MME, without substantially redefining the research positioning.

P1.justification: The existing results narrative is substantially rewritten and reorganized into separate Key Observations, Inter-task/Intra-task Analysis, and Validity sections. Cleaning and introductory comparison passages are expanded, and the appendix presentation gains dedicated validation and documentation sections. Much background prose and the example/datasheet material remain, but the empirical narrative undergoes substantial restructuring.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the main results presentation with a colored 26-model matrix and moves the expanded clean-subtask tables into Appendix A. It removes the original style heatmap and question-type example panel, adds clustering and KMMD heatmaps, radar charts, audit tables, and failure-case panels, and substantially reworks the appendix leaderboards. Pipeline diagrams, metadata displays, and most example figures are retained with layout changes.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct measurement of annotation correctness. v3's 7.7K-image audit, reported 2.2% error rate, and score comparison after excluding errors substantially strengthen that evidence. Blind and distribution comparisons further examine benchmark validity, while broader model comparisons and diagnostic analyses improve its usefulness. These gains outweigh the loss of some detailed result breakdowns, although filtering based on top-performing models leaves a selection-bias concern, and blind performance alone does not establish freedom from data leakage.
